title: [Triton/Gluon] Add a16w4 MoE tuned dispatch and gfx942 DSv4.1 tables
body:
## Summary

`get_kernel_config_triton` hardcodes `block_k=256`, `block_n=512` and `num_stages=1` for every architecture. Those suit CDNA4's 160 KiB of LDS; CDNA3 has 64 KiB, so the gfx942 prefill tile runs at very low occupancy.

This routes the kernel through the tuned dispatch that `a8w4` already uses and ships a gfx942 table for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 and TP8.

- `get_moe_dispatch("A16W4", get_arch(), "triton")`, keyed by `bm<block_m>_n<N>_k<K>`
- `configs/gfx942/triton/moe/a16w4/DEFAULT.json`, 8 entries

`get_moe_dispatch` returns `{}` when no file is shipped, so untuned architectures are unaffected. On gfx942 only the 8 listed prefill shapes change; decode (`block_m` 16/32) and unlisted shapes keep the existing defaults.

## Results

MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, E=384, topk=6.

| entry | stock | tuned | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bm128_n1536_k5120` | 16.484 ms | 4.219 ms | 3.91x |
| `bm128_n5120_k768` | 8.131 ms | 1.924 ms | 4.22x |
| `bm128_n1024_k5120` | 11.275 ms | 2.688 ms | 4.20x |
| `bm128_n5120_k512` | 5.288 ms | 1.463 ms | 3.67x |
| `bm64_n1536_k5120` | 2.155 ms | 1.291 ms | 1.68x |
| `bm64_n5120_k768` | 1.152 ms | 0.660 ms | 1.75x |
| `bm64_n1024_k5120` | 1.477 ms | 0.882 ms | 1.65x |
| `bm64_n5120_k512` | 0.839 ms | 0.503 ms | 1.68x |

End to end via vLLM (`--moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16`, random 65536 in / 512 out, concurrency 8, TP=4, 3 repeats, CV 0.14%):

| metric | stock | tuned | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Output throughput | 97.35 tok/s | 111.88 tok/s | +14.9% |
| TPOT mean | 55.70 ms | 44.80 ms | -19.6% |

## Notes on Tuning

No a16w4 tile tuner exists in-tree, so the entries come from a sweep over all six knobs the kernel forwards to the launch.

Worth knowing when adding shapes:

- `block_k=64` compiles only with `matrix_instr_nonkdim=32`, and it wins at `block_m=128` on most shapes. Sweeping with `nonkdim` fixed hides it entirely.
- `block_n=256` won on every shape; the stock 512 never did.

## Tests

- All 8 entries verified resolving to the measured tiles against a live install; decode and unlisted shapes confirmed returning the existing defaults.
- Tuned vs stock output differs by exactly 0.5 bf16 ULP, caused by `block_k` changing the K-split. `block_n`, `num_stages` and `num_warps` are bit-identical.
- GSM8K 8-shot (200 examples, chat endpoint): 0.905 exact_match (flexible-extract) on both the tuned and stock-tile arms are identical.

## Limits

- Measured on MI325X. gfx942 also covers MI300X, which shares the 64 KiB LDS but not the memory bandwidth; untested there.
- TP4 and TP8 only. TP2 needs ~287 GiB/GPU for this model and cannot load.
- Keys use the **padded** intermediate: the per-rank shard is rounded up to a multiple of 256 before reaching the kernel (TP4 576 -> 768, TP8 288 -> 512), so gemm1 is `n=2*

## Summary

Add `torch.symm_mem` (mori backend) as a peer-buffer transport for gfx1250
custom all-reduce, and extend gfx1250 kernels to world_size {2, 4, 6, 8}.

### symm_mem transport (opt-in, gfx1250)
- Enable with `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_USE_SYMM_MEM=1`; reuses the gfx1250 pointer-list ops.
- 64 B collective probe: all ranks vote, then fall back to VMM/IPC together (no hang).
- After the probe passes, allocation/rendezvous failures raise on every rank.
- Cross-node and `expandable_segments` guards are evaluated after the transport is final.
- `register_*_buffer` raises on this transport (would share a stale copy).

### gfx1250 world_size 6/8
- `DISPATCH_NGPUS_1250` + `check_ngpus()` (init-time check); `kMaxNgpus = 8`.
- LL scratch sized by world_size (32 MiB @ TP2, 128 MiB @ TP8).
- AG rejects outputs past the int32 index range.
- `meta_size_gfx1250(world_size=8)`: backward compatible default.

### Others
- all2all: skip mori shmem init on gfx125x (EP uses cco there).
- test: `--transport {auto,symm}` in `test_custom_allreduce.py`.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Fix pa_decode compile error with newer Triton: don't index scalar alpha
body:
## Motivation

On current Triton main, `paged_attention_decode` no longer compiles for query group size 1:

```
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 99:15:
        acc *= alpha[:, None]
ValueError: too many indices for tensor of rank 0
```

triton-lang/triton#10429 ("[BC-Breaking] Reject too many tensor slice indices", merged 2026-09-24) makes over-indexing a tensor an error. It breaks `bench_pa_decode.py`, `bench_la_paged_decode.py` and `test_pa_decode.py` whenever the `*_wo_dot` path is taken.

## Technical Details

In the four `*_wo_dot` kernels, `max_logit` starts as `float("-inf")` and stays a scalar, so `alpha` is a rank-0 tensor and `alpha[:, None]` indexes it twice. Older Triton accepted this and broadcast the result. Multiplying by the scalar directly broadcasts over `acc` the same way, so behavior is unchanged.

Kernels changed (one line each):
- `_paged_attn_decode_v1_wo_dot_kernel`
- `_paged_attn_decode_v2_wo_dot_kernel`
- `_paged_attn_decode_v1_wo_dot_kernel_per_token_quant`
- `_paged_attn_decode_v2_wo_dot_kernel_per_token_quant`

The `*_w_dot` kernels are left alone: their `max_logit` is a `[QUERY_GRP_SZ_POW2]` vector, so `alpha[:, None]` is valid there.

Also adds `test_paged_attn_v2` (see the Copilot thread). `test_paged_attn` stops at 1024 tokens, a single partition, so no checked-in test reached the V2 kernels. The new test:
- runs `SEQ_LEN=4096` (four partitions) for MHA and GQA, with bf16 and fp8 KV caches
- checks the output against the reference
- spies on `paged_attn_decode_v2`, so it fails if a dispatch change routes these cases back to V1

## Test Plan

On MI350X (gfx950), with a Triton main wheel built from triton-lang/triton@072983377d, which includes #10429:

1. Without the kernel fix: `test_pa_decode.py -k "test_paged_attn and not per_token"` and the new `-k test_paged_attn_v2`.
2. With the fix: the new test, then the full `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_pa_decode.py`.

## Test Result

- Without the fix: fails with `too many indices for tensor of rank 0`. In the new test, the 4 MHA cases, which reach `_paged_attn_decode_v2_wo_dot_kernel`, fail; the 4 GQA cases pass.
- With the fix: `test_paged_attn_v2` gives 8 passed. The full file gives `824 passed, 144 skipped`; the skips are the file's own `pytest.skip` cases.
- All four modified kernels were compiled and exercised.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] Route GLM-5 qkv_a_proj decode tiers to the triton split-K kernel on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

GLM-5's `qkv_a_proj` is `N=2624, K=6144`. At decode sizes every gfx950/256 row for that shape selects a CK blockscale kernel whose tile leaves about 123 workgroups on 256 CUs, so the GEMM never fills the device and runs at the weight's bandwidth floor. The triton split-K preshuffled kernel fills it, but the shape has no triton config, so `--libtype all` never proposes one and the tuner cannot find it.

## Technical Details

- Replace the gfx950/256 `M = 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64` rows for `N=2624 K=6144` with `triton` rows.
- Drop the `M = 2` and `M = 48` CK rows. `getPaddedM` rounds `M <= 256` up to a multiple of 16 at `gl=0` and to `nextPow2` at `gl=1`, and the probe returns the first tier that hits. With the `M = 2` row present, `M = 2` stays on CK; with the `M = 48` row present, it catches `M = 33-48` before the probe reaches the `M = 64` triton tier. Both are measured below.
- Add `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE_PRESHUFFLED-N=2624-K=6144.json` with a split-K config per M bucket.

## Test Plan

Measured on MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU) against `main` at `766e70d19`, through the production `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` dispatch, not by comparing `us` columns. Each arm is a separate process with `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BLOCKSCALE_BPRESHUFFLE` pointed at the old or the new table (both `get_config_file` and `get_CKGEMM_config` are `lru_cache`d, so one process cannot see two tables). Each arm reports the `libtype` the dispatch actually chose, so a result cannot come from silently running the same kernel twice. CUDA-graph timed, best of five 20-replay rounds.

The benchmark rotates over 32 distinct weights. A single 16 MB weight stays resident in cache and inverts the ranking — CK measures 6.4-7.0 us that way and looks faster — but a decode step walks 78 different `qkv_a_proj` weights, so the bandwidth-bound regime is the one that matters. Arm order was alternated (`a` then `b`) to rule out ordering effects.

## Test Result

| M | CK (a / b) us | triton (a / b) us | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 14.67 / 14.62 | 6.46 / 6.47 | 0.44x |
| 2 | 14.72 / 14.65 | 7.77 / 7.79 | 0.53x |
| 4 | 14.67 / 14.59 | 7.91 / 7.90 | 0.54x |
| 8 | 14.64 / 14.64 | 8.00 / 7.99 | 0.55x |
| 16 | 14.54 / 14.54 | 8.41 / 8.42 | 0.58x |
| 32 | 14.45 / 14.47 | 9.77 / 9.71 | 0.67x |
| 33 | 14.40 / 14.39 | 9.93 / 10.01 | 0.69x |
| 48 | 14.34 / 14.24 | 10.32 / 10.33 | 0.72x |
| 64 | 14.34 / 14.20 | 10.91 / 10.94 | 0.76x |

The two passes differ by at most 0.5%, and the arms' ranges are disjoint at every M.

**The two dropped rows.** `M = 2` now resolves through `gl=0` to the `M = 16` triton row, and `M = 33` / `M = 48` fall through to the `M = 64` triton row. Those are the `M = 2, 33, 48` lines above: each is faster than the CK row it replaces, so the deletions are not merely reachability changes.

**Numerics.** Relative L2 against a torch fp32 reference is 1.2e-4 to 3.1e-4 for both arms at every M — the two kernels are equivalent. Per-element relative error is not reported because a `K=6144` fp8 dot product cancels to a value far below its terms, so a near-zero output element inflates that ratio without any loss of accuracy.

**Control shape.** `N=6144 K=2048`, which this table does not tune, resolves identically in both arms and times 11.38 / 11.04 / 10.10 us against 11.39 / 11.07 / 10.08 us at `M = 1 / 16 / 64`. No other shape is disturbed.

End to end this ships in a GLM-5.3 MXFP4 stack together with other changes, so no isolated serving number is claimed here.

title: [FlyDSL] [MLA] DeepSeek-V4 fp8 MLA decode (v4 nm) in one FlyDSL launch on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 fp8 MLA decode (v4 nm) on gfx950 runs the asm `mla_a8w8_qh64_qseqlen1_gqaratio64_nm.co` plus a separate split-merge kernel. This PR adds a FlyDSL version that does both in one launch. It is faster than the best asm configuration in every cell of the kernel matrix, and it lowers DSv4-Pro 8K/1K ITL by 0.6–2.6%.

## Technical Details

- New entry points in `aiter.ops.flydsl`. `aiter.mla` is unchanged, so nothing is routed by default.
  - `flydsl_mla_decode_fwd_v4_nm`: drop-in for `mla_decode_fwd_v4_nm` (bf16 output). It covers every pair the asm ships: H 16/32/64/128 at msq 1, and H16 at msq 2/4.
  - `flydsl_mla_v4_decode_fused`: the same kernel with an inverse-RoPE + wo_a mxfp8 quant epilogue.
  - `q_kv_bounds` + `flydsl_mla_v4_grouped_verify_meta`: native grouped DSpark verify (sgl-project/sglang#41120-style), one stream per request with per-draft key ranges.
- A graph-capture-safe host plan picks the tile loop (K / RP / RQ / RD / Q16) and the split count for each (H, msq, batch, stream kind). The split merge runs inside the same launch through a ticket protocol that needs no co-residency.
- Requires `flydsl==0.3.4.1`, the current pin.
- Known gaps: a few shapes outside the matrix are still slower than asm, for example H128 B100 ragged L4096 (1.17x) and H16 B17 L16–32K (~1.1x). Follow-up work is in progress.

## Test Plan

It also checks the contracts: empty rows return NaN, padding bytes are never read, CUDA-graph replay is bit-exact, B=0 is a no-op, and batches over 4096 merge groups run unsplit.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] Add a tuned gfx1101 MHA config, split small_head/default
body:
> *Rewritten on 2026-09-10, after the branch was force-pushed from `c27cabd7` to `ec3af272`. The earlier description covered the flat-layout file and values that no longer hold; that revision and the review anchored to it are unchanged in the history. What moved and why is in the comment below.* ## Motivation `aiter.ops.triton.attention.mha.flash_attn_func` cannot run at all on gfx1101 (RDNA3). `_get_config` resolves `configs/{arch}/triton/attention/mha/DEFAULT.json`, and with no per-arch file and no fallback the call raises ```text FileNotFoundError: Required config file doesn't exist: aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx1101/triton/attention/mha/DEFAULT.json ``` before any kernel is compiled. gfx1101 is in `RDNA_ARCHS`, so the architecture is declared supported while the default MHA path is unreachable on it. This PR is the narrow remedy for the one architecture I can measure on. ## What changed since the approval on 2026-08-06 This PR was approved at `c27cabd7`, and **that revision no longer holds**, so the branch has been rewritten rather than merged as approved. Two things moved underneath it: the config layout (#5018 / #5019 deleted the flat path without a fallback) and the kernel (#3936, #4414). Re-measured against today's `main`, the approved `fwd/default` is **1.274x slower on `head_dim` 128**, and on `head_dim` 64 it no longer establishes a gain — the intervals overlap the donor's. What moved is the donor, not the candidate: the inherited gfx1151 entry became faster on today's kernel while the tuned one stood still. Numerics did not move at all, so a correctness re-verification passes with digit-identical residuals — re-verifying rather than re-measuring would have merged the regression. Rather than withdraw the tuning, this revision **splits it in two**, which removes the regression instead of trading one shape against another. ## Technical Details One new file, `aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx1101/triton/attention/mha/DEFAULT.json`, in the nested layout from #5019. 101 lines added, nothing removed, no code touched. Nine of the eleven entries are byte-identical to `gfx1151/triton/attention/mha/DEFAULT.json`, the nearest tuned architecture. Two forward entries are tuned on gfx1101 instead of inherited: ```text fwd/default BLOCK_M 64 -> 128, num_warps 4 -> 8, num_stages 2 -> 3 (vs. the gfx1151 donor) fwd/small_head BLOCK_M 128, num_warps 4, num_stages 1 (new key, no donor equivalent) ``` `fwd/small_head` is the bucket added in #4414 for `16 < head_dim_v <= 64`. Because it is opt-in per architecture by the presence of the key, this remains a data-only change that cannot affect any other architecture. The split is needed because the two `head_dim` ranges want a different `num_warps`, and `_get_config` already discriminates on exactly that axis. Two independent coarse sweeps, one per range, selected these two entries separately — the numbers are below. 📌 **The comment on that bucket does not describe this architecture, and these values should not be read as agreeing with it.** It states that `16 < d <= 64` suffers a `num_stages=1` pipelining pathology which `num_stages=3` cures. On gfx1101 the ordering is the opposite: on the tuned `M128 / N32 / w4` tile, `num_stages` 1 / 2 / 3 measured 2.346 / 2.429 / 2.450 ms. If that comment is meant as an invariant rather than as an observation about the architectures tuned so far, it changes the answer here, and I would rather be told than assume.
⚠️ num_stages is Triton-version-dependent on this architecture, so these values should not be assumed to carry backwards — click for why Under the Triton used here, `use_async_copy` defaults to `arch in ["gfx950", "gfx1250"]` and `is_pingpong_schedule_enabled` admits only gfx942 and gfx950 (`triton/backends/amd/compiler.py:43` and `:33`), so gfx1101 gets neither. `num_stages` therefore means classic software pipelining into **registers** only, which is why it can trade against `BLOCK_M` and why the answer differs between the two head-dim ranges. Under Triton 3.7.1 the same knob had a different gate — `use_async_copy` read the env knob without testing the arch — so these numbers should not be assumed to carry backwards.
`fwd/dropout_or_fp32`, both `pe` entries and both backward sections are inherited unchanged; only the forward path was exercised, so no claim is made about backward. ## Test Plan Windows native ROCm, RX 7800 XT (gfx1101, RDNA3, 60 CU), AITER checkout on `PYTHONPATH` with no install, `AITER_TRITON_ONLY` implicit on win32. **Every number below was measured on one software stack**: torch `2.15.0a0+rocm10.1.0a20260822`, HIP 7.16.26332, `triton-windows` **3.8.0.post28**, a Windows build of Triton 3.8.0 and the newest release available. Older stacks are deliberately not reported, so that no row here describes a configuration that is no longer current. fp16, seed 424242. Each point is the median of 20 timed iterations after 5 warmups with `torch.cuda.synchronize()` per iteration. Sweeps are single-shot rankings over a grid; every claimed ratio comes from a series of **10 independent repeats**, and is claimed only where the `[min, max]` intervals across those repeats are **disjoint**. Where they overlap this is stated and nothing is claimed. Ratios are against the gfx1151 donor entry, since inheriting is the alternative to this file. Two shape sets. Diffusion attention: SDXL self-attention `(2, 4096, 4096, 10, 64)`, `head_dim` 64, and a Flux joint-attention shape `(1, 4608, 4608, 24, 128)`, `head_dim` 128. LLM prefill, `causal=True`, GQA, batch 1, head dims from `op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/utils/model_configs.json` (`hidden_size / num_attention_heads`); the sequence lengths are not in that file and are my choice, 4096 and 16384.
⚠️ The upstream MHA test and benchmark harness cannot run on this host, so its shape set is used with my own measuring path — click for the chain `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_mha.py` and `bench_mha.py` both reach `aiter.dtypes`, which `aiter/__init__.py` binds only in the non-`AITER_TRITON_ONLY` branch, and the JIT path below it ends in `RuntimeError("ROCm version file not found")`. The upstream *shape set* is therefore used with my own measuring path rather than the upstream harness. This is independent of the present change, and I preferred not to introduce a workaround into the verification being reported.
## Test Result ### The defect is still present on the current base With the new file removed from the checkout, on `main` @ `12620102` and the stack above: ```text FileNotFoundError: Required config file doesn't exist: .../aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx1101/triton/attention/mha/DEFAULT.json _triton_kernels/attention/mha.py:955 -> utils/config_utils.py:50 ``` It is raised on the first call and on every later call in the same process. On that base the architectures that do have an MHA config are gfx942, gfx950, gfx1151 and gfx1250. Two escape hatches work on the same host and the same shape: passing `config=` explicitly, and `mha_set_impl("dao_ai")`. Both return `max abs 6.470e-05` against the fp32 reference, against `6.013e-05` for torch's own fp16 SDPA measured in the same process. The kernel therefore runs correctly on this architecture, and it is only the config lookup that makes the default path unreachable. ### Routing and correctness Verified on `main` @ `12620102` with this file applied, each entry in a **separate process** because `_get_config` memoises. `head_dim` 64 routing to `small_head` and `head_dim` 128 routing to `default` is the behaviour the split depends on.
All six forward entries resolve as intended, max abs 6.469e-05 to 7.008e-05 — click for the per-entry output ```text v_head_dim 128, fp16 -> default max abs vs fp32 reference 7.008e-05 v_head_dim 64, fp16 -> small_head max abs vs fp32 reference 6.469e-05 v_head_dim 64, fp16 + dropout -> dropout_or_fp32 finite, dropout active v_head_dim 64, fp32 -> dropout_or_fp32 max abs 8.643e-07 v_head_dim 64, pe -> pe max abs 6.685e-05 v_head_dim 64, pe + dropout -> pe_dropout_or_fp32 finite, dropout active ```
Every configuration measured in this campaign produced an identical maximum absolute difference per shape, the inherited one included, so tile parameters have no numerical effect on this kernel and the choice is purely a performance decision. ### How the two entries were selected One coarse sweep per head-dim range, 72 candidates each over `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x num_warps x num_stages`, ranked on that range's shape. The two sweeps are independent and each selected the entry this PR ships for its own range. | sweep shape | best of 72 | ms | vs. donor | approved `M128 w4 s1` on the same shape | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `head_dim` 64 | `M128 N32 w4 s1` = this PR's `small_head` | 2.346 | 0.974 | it is that entry | | `head_dim` 128 | `M128 N32 w8 s3` = this PR's `default` | 6.444 | 0.933 | 8.619, i.e. 1.25 | The separating knob is `num_warps`: at `head_dim` 128 the same tile measures 8.619 ms at `w4 s1` against 6.657 ms at `w8 s1`, while at `head_dim` 64 the ordering reverses. A refine stage over `PRELOAD_V` and `waves_per_eu` on the three best candidates produced no cell that beat `M128 N32 w8 s3 pv0 we1` on `head_dim` 128. Three of the 72 candidates on the `head_dim` 128 shape are unusable on this architecture, and the failure is the expected one: `out of resource: shared memory, Required: 69632 (resp. 73728), Hardware limit: 65536`. ### `head_dim` 128 — the regression and its removal 10 repeats per configuration, and the whole series run twice. `[min, max]` over the repeats in ms, ratio of medians against the donor in brackets. | series | donor `M64 w4 s2` | approved `M128 w4 s1` | **this PR's `default`, `M128 w8 s3`** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | run 1 | [6.805, 7.028] | [8.575, 8.776] (1.273) ❌ | **[6.437, 6.503] (0.944)** ✅ | | run 2 | [6.787, 7.034] | [8.698, 8.789] (1.274) ❌ | **[6.411, 6.513] (0.943)** ✅ | ✅ / ❌ = intervals disjoint from the donor's. The two runs agree to the third significant figure, and the same `M128 w8 s3` entry costs **1.070–1.077** on `head_dim` 64 — which is the reason one `fwd/default` cannot serve both ranges. ### LLM prefill shapes, `causal=True`, GQA, batch 1 Ratios against the donor, whose median in ms is given for scale.
All ten shapes: the entry this file routes to is the faster candidate in every row, significantly so in all ten — click for the table | shape | head_dim | donor ms | `M128 w4 s1` | `M128 w8 s3` | routed by this file to | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | llama3-8B, sq 4096 | 128 | 3.885 | 1.331 ❌ | 0.951 *(overlap)* | `default` | | llama3-8B, sq 16384 | 128 | 56.949 | 1.316 ❌ | **0.904** ✅ | `default` | | mixtral-7B, sq 4096 | 128 | 3.950 | 1.331 ❌ | **0.935** ✅ | `default` | | mixtral-7B, sq 16384 | 128 | 57.483 | 1.285 ❌ | **0.895** ✅ | `default` | | kimi-k2.5 tp4, sq 4096 | 112 | 8.344 | 1.298 ❌ | **0.892** ✅ | `default` | | kimi-k2.5 tp4, sq 16384 | 112 | 143.159 | 1.136 ❌ | **0.775** ✅ | `default` | | deepseek-V3, sq 4096 | 56 | 8.746 | **0.828** ✅ | 0.924 ✅ | `small_head` | | deepseek-V3, sq 16384 | 56 | 167.621 | **0.644** ✅ | 0.714 ✅ | `small_head` | | glm-4.7-fp8 tp4, sq 4096 | 53 | 5.964 | **0.915** ✅ | 1.019 *(overlap)* | `small_head` | | glm-4.7-fp8 tp4, sq 16384 | 53 | 93.844 | **0.852** ✅ | **0.922** ✅ | `small_head` |
In every row the entry this file routes the shape to is the faster of the two candidates, and in nine of the ten it is significantly faster than the donor. Comparing the two candidates directly, their `[min, max]` intervals are **disjoint in all ten rows** — the routing decision is significant on every shape in the set, even where the winner's margin over the donor is not. This set matters because #3560 tuned the donor on `n=112` LLM shapes, so choosing `fwd/default` on diffusion shapes replaces an LLM-derived value with a diffusion-derived one. The measurement says the two families do not disagree on this card: both want `num_warps 8` at `head_dim` 112–128, and the axis that separates them is `head_dim`, not workload. ### `head_dim` 64, `fwd/small_head` The LLM rows above are the evidence for this entry, and they are the only significant evidence for it. On the diffusion shape it ranked first of 72 candidates in the sweep, but across 10 repeats it measures 0.933 and 0.936 with intervals that **overlap** the donor's in both runs, so no gain is claimed there. The entry is nonetheless the right one for its range, and the comparison that establishes that is against the alternative rather than against the donor. Giving `fwd/default` to both ranges measures 1.070–1.077 on the diffusion `head_dim` 64 shape, and on the four `head_dim` 53–56 LLM shapes it is slower than `M128 w4 s1` by 0.924 vs 0.828, 0.714 vs 0.644, 1.019 vs 0.915 and 0.922 vs 0.852 — disjoint intervals in all four. ## What this does not establish Batch > 1, the `varlen` / `thd` layout, sliding window, and the decode phase (`seqlen_q = 1`) were not measured. Forward path only; both backward sections are inherited. One card, one host and one software stack — no other RDNA or CDNA part is available to me, and nothing here is a claim about gfx1151, whose values this PR does not change. A cross-attention shape `(2, 4096, 77, 10, 64)` was measured and is deliberately not reported: the donor's own timing on it varies by 31 % across repeats on this host, which is far above every other shape in the set, so it discriminates nothing in either direction. A cross-architecture fallback for the same reachability defect is a separate change and is deliberately not bundled here. I am happy to file it separately if that is wanted.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Bugfix] Mask the split-K tail in the blockscale GEMMs
body:
## Summary

`compute_splitk_params` rounds `SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE` up to a multiple of `BLOCK_SIZE_K` and recomputes `NUM_KSPLIT`, so `NUM_KSPLIT * SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE` can exceed K: the last partition starts inside K and runs past it. The blockscale kernels' `EVEN_K` heuristic only checks `K % BLOCK_SIZE_K == 0`, so that tail is loaded without masks. The output is wrong or NaN, and the stray reads can fault.

Example: the gfx942 default A8W8 config uses `NUM_KSPLIT=8` for M <= 64. With K=384 that becomes 2 splits of 256. The second split covers [256, 512), and the tile at [384, 512) is read unmasked.

Relative error against a dequantized reference (MI325X, N=6144, via `gemm_a8w8_blockscale` with the default config):

| K | M=1 | M=16 | M=64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 384, before | 11.8 | NaN | 0.58 |
| 640, before | 0.025 | 0.44 | 0.92 |
| 384 / 640, after | 0.025 | 0.026 | 0.026 |

0.025 is the fp8 quantization noise floor, the same value K=768 and K=1024 give before the fix.

We hit this serving `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` with SGLang at TP8 on MI325X. The shared-expert `down_proj` has K=384 per rank, so the model decoded token 0 and CUDA-graph capture hit `Memory access fault by GPU`.

## Fix

`EVEN_K` also requires `K % SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE == 0`, in `_gemm_a8w8_blockscale_kernel` and `_gemm_a16w8_blockscale_kernel`. Without split-K, `SPLITK_BLOCK_SIZE == K`, so behavior is unchanged there. The preshuffle kernels are left alone: their wrappers size the split differently, and the a16w8 preshuffle kernel has no masked path.

## Tests

- `test_gemm_a8w8_blockscale.py`: shapes `(M, 6144, K)` for M in {1, 16, 64} and K in {640, 896}, plus `test_gemm_splitk_tail`, which forces `NUM_KSPLIT=8`.
- `test_gemm_a16w8_blockscale.py`: `test_gemm_splitk_tail`. The default gfx942 a16w8 config doesn't split K, so the test forces it.
- gfx942: 9 of the new cases fail before the fix; all 16 pass after. The existing a8w8 and a16w8 subsets still pass (212 + 26). `test_legacy_gluon_import_path_warns` fails on this box both before and after (unrelated).
- Only validated on gfx942 with the triton backend. The new shapes also run the gluon backend on gfx950 / gfx1250.

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.
Hyperloom was optimizing `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` on MI325X (TP8).

title: [FlyDSL] Fuse the GDN gated RMSNorm into the out_proj GEMM for decode
body:
## Summary

Add `flydsl_gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj`, a FlyDSL kernel for gfx950 that runs the gated RMSNorm of a Gated DeltaNet layer and the bf16 `out_proj` GEMM as one kernel at decode. On MI355X at K = 2048 and N = 8192 (`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` at TP8) it takes 8.1 to 12.1 µs for 1 to 5 tokens inside a HIP graph, where the separate norm and GEMM take 11.6 to 16.4 µs.

## Background

At decode, every Gated DeltaNet layer (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8) runs `RMSNormGated` and then the unquantized `out_proj` GEMM:

```
y[t, h, :] = bf16(x[t, h, :] * rsqrt(mean(x[t, h, :]^2) + eps) * w * silu(z[t, h, :]))
out[t, :] = y[t].flatten() @ W.T
```

`w` has `head_dim` values and is shared by all heads. The norm writes `y` to HBM and the GEMM reads it back. At 1 to 5 tokens the GEMM is bound by the weight read, so the norm kernel and the gap before the GEMM are mostly extra time.

## What this PR does

- `aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj.py` is the kernel. One workgroup owns `cols_per_wave * waves_per_block` output columns. Each wave issues the loads of its weight rows first and the loads of `x` and `z` after them. The waves of the workgroup then compute the gated norm of all tokens into LDS as bf16. After one barrier, each wave computes its output columns with `v_dot2_f32_bf16` and reduces each column over the 64 lanes. `y` is rounded to bf16 before the multiply, as in the unfused path.
- `aiter/ops/flydsl/gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj.py` is the wrapper. `flydsl_gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj(x, z, norm_weight, weight, eps)` picks a tile per token count and caches the compiled kernels. `flydsl_gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj_supported(num_tokens, num_heads, head_dim, out_features, dtype)` returns False where the kernel was not clearly faster than the separate norm and GEMM, so a caller can fall back there. It accepts K from 1024 to 4096, the measured range: up to 8 tokens at K = 1024 and up to 5 tokens at K = 2048 and K = 4096.
- `aiter/ops/flydsl/__init__.py` exports both functions.
- `op_tests/test_flydsl_gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj.py` checks the result against a torch reference with the same bf16 rounding and times the kernel. It covers the supported token counts at K = 1024, 2048, and 4096, one N that needs the smaller fallback tile, and the path where the wrapper allocates the output.

The wrapper supports gfx950, `head_dim` 128, bf16, contiguous tensors, and the SiLU gate. It reads the arch of the GPU in use, not `GPU_ARCHS`. Other shapes and archs return False from `_supported`.

## Validation

MI355X, ROCm 7.2.4, torch 2.10.0, FlyDSL 0.3.4.1, on top of main at 8253efc.

Correctness: `python3 op_tests/test_flydsl_gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj.py` passes all 27 default shapes with an error count of 0 at `rtol = atol = 1e-2`. AITER's `validate-kernel-pr` skill passes on this head. It applies the patch to 8253efc, runs the op test and four more shapes (`-s 4,5120,2048`, `3,2560,1536`, `5,6144,3584`, and `2,4104,2048`) on an idle MI355X, and its execution receipt shows that the calls reached `flydsl_gdn_gated_rmsnorm_out_proj`. Its index-width scan lists five products without 64-bit widening. The only one on the device is the vector index into `x` and `z`, which is at most 4159 because the LDS limit keeps `num_tokens * K` at or below 32768.

Time per call inside a HIP graph, in µs. Every call reads a different copy of the weight, at least 768 MB in total, so the weight always comes from HBM, as in a real decode step. The unfused path is the gated norm compiled by `torch.compile` followed by vLLM's unquantized GEMM dispatch with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. At these shapes it runs `wvSplitK` for 1 to 5 tokens and AITER's `tgemm.mm` from 6 tokens.

| Tokens | K=2048, N=8192 unfused | fused | K=4096, N=8192 unfused | fused | K=1024, N=4096 unfused | fused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 11.61 | 8.14 | 18.47 | 13.53 | 6.63 | 4.71 |
| 2 | 11.83 | 8.53 | 23.29 | 14.35 | 6.79 | 4.85 |
| 3 | 12.11 | 9.12 | 19.70 | 16.74 | 7.57 | 5.93 |
| 4 | 16.38 | 9.66 | 19.46 | 17.57 | 7.34 | 5.21 |
| 5 | 12.77 | 12.06 | 20.08 | 19.09 | 8.14 | 6.43 |
| 6 | 13.34 | (13.31) | 19.81 | (22.54) | 7.85 | 6.88 |
| 7 | 13.06 | (14.06) | | | 9.46 | 7.25 |
| 8 | 13.01 | (15.50) | | | 12.08 | 7.23 |

Values in parentheses are measured, but `_supported` returns False there. K = 1024 with N = 4096 is `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B` at TP8. In this test the unfused path is the norm kernel and the GEMM. In the vLLM server, Inductor also runs a copy of the norm output into the GEMM input, so the saving there is larger, see below.

The op test also prints a `gemm_a16w16` time. That GEMM runs on a `y` computed before timing, without the norm kernel. For 1 to 5 tokens vLLM runs `wvSplitK` and not `gemm_a16w16`. The table above is the comparison with the path it replaces.

The final ISA from the FlyDSL dump has no VGPR or SGPR spills and no scratch in any of the 27 default kernels. At K = 2048 the kernel uses 61 to 126 VGPRs for 1 to 5 tokens. LDS is `num_tokens * K * 2` bytes.

End to end in vLLM: vllm-project/vllm#58802 uses this kernel in the GDN layers. On `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` at TP8, median TPOT drops by 3.5% at 1 concurrent request (14.84 to 14.31 ms), by 2.8% at 2, and by 3.6% at 4, and gsm8k does not change. ## Motivation

- NemotronH's MoE layers use Squared ReLU (`relu(x)^2`) as their activation function. Tier 1 (#5689) added a standalone `relu2` kernel so aiter could compute this activation directly instead of falling back to eager PyTorch, but that PR only covered the simple elementwise case, not the fused MoE GEMM path.

- The fused MoE GEMM path (`csrc/ck_tile_gemm_moe_2stages/`) didn't support relu2 at all. 

- This PR adds real relu2 support to the fused MoE GEMM path, so NemotronH's MoE layers can run through aiter's fast CK-Tile kernels instead of falling back to a legacy path that doesn't support relu2 at all.

This is Tier 2 of a 3-PR series adding end-to-end relu2 support:

1. #5689 -- standalone aiter elementwise kernel (no dependencies)
2. This PR -- aiter CK-Tile fused MoE GEMM support for relu2 (depends
   on Tier 1)

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add 3D neighborhood flash attention (na3d_flash)
body:
## Motivation

Video diffusion models such as LTX-2.5 use 3D neighborhood attention in
the VAE diffusion decoder: each token at grid position (t, h, w) attends
only to its (KT x KH x KW) neighbors rather than the full sequence. This
PR adds a BF16 MFMA flash-style kernel for that operation targeting gfx942
and gfx950, plus a reference, tests and benchmarks.

**Use case example**
LTX-2.5 Diffusion decoder attention processor [in xDiT](https://github.com/xdit-project/xDiT/pull/773) inference framework.

## Technical Details

Six new files:

**`aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/attention/na3d_flash.py`**

`_na3d_flash_fwd`:  flash attention inner kernel.
- Inward border-shift: every window contains exactly KT x KH x KW keys
- Q loaded once into registers; K/V iterated over KT x KH rows
- Online softmax in log2 space (exp2, log2(e) folded into scale factor)
- Flat KT x KH loop with static trip count enables Triton's software pipeliner

**`aiter/ops/triton/attention/na3d_flash.py`**

`na3d_flash_attn(q, k, v, kernel_size)` -
public launcher. Input/output shape: (B, T, H, W, NH, HD) bfloat16,
Q pre-scaled by head_dim**-0.5.
Tuned configs provided for gfx950/gfx942 for ltx-2.5 model default shapes.

**`aiter/op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_na3d_flash.py`**

- `_na3d_sdpa_exact(q, k, v, kernel_size, w_offset=0)` - Reference method. Exact per-query
neighborhood SDPA. Groups queries by shared relative-window geometry and
calls `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` per group with a cached additive mask.
With w_offset=0 and full q/k/v this is equivalent to a per-query FP32
reference but runs on the GPU. With w_offset>0, q is a W sub-slice and
k/v are the full tensors; neighborhood bounds use global W coordinates.

- `test_na3d_flash`: 9 shapes (5 LTX-2.5 default + 5 edge cases); reference
  is `_na3d_sdpa_exact`, atol=5e-2
- `test_na3d_sdpa_exact_vs_ref`: 6 small shapes; cross-checks `_na3d_sdpa_exact`
  against the FP32 per-query loop

**`op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_na3d_flash.py`**
- Performance benchmark for 3D neighborhood flash attention (na3d_flash) that compares against `_na3d_sdpa_exact` reference method from `aiter/op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_na3d_flash.py`.
- Measures TFLOPS and TB/s per shape

- **`aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx950/triton/attention/na3d_flash/DEFAULT.json`**: Tuned config for gfx950
- **`aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx942/triton/attention/na3d_flash/DEFAULT.json`**: Tuned config for gfx942

## Test Plan

Run pytest on gfx950:

    pytest op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_na3d_flash.py -v

## Test Result

All tests pass on gfx950 (MI350X) in ~30 s.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add fused Qwen3-Next GDN prefill (gfx950 Gluon) with fp8 group-quant epilogue
body:
A single fused op for the Qwen3-Next gated delta-net *prefill* chain (causal_conv1d_split_qkv -> fused gating -> fp32 chunked delta scan -> gated RMSNorm -> per-head group-128 FP8 quant), replacing the four-kernel path with a tight set of Gluon launches that fuse the work intra-kernel and drop the intermediate HBM traffic. The FP8 activations a block-FP8 out_proj consumes are emitted by the epilogue launch (no separate quant kernel).

Support is reported, not asserted: fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz_supported gates on gfx950, Triton >= 3.8 (Gluon dialect), and an in-range (tokens, batch)/dtype contract, so callers fall back to the four-kernel chain instead of crashing. Prefill spans a wide token range, so it dispatches one of four autotuned M-tile schedules. The Gluon/HIP tiles import lazily on dispatch, keeping the module and the support predicate importable on any platform.

Tests: pure-torch fp32 sequential-scan reference (deliberately not the chunked algorithm) at the kernel's bf16 rounding boundaries; 9/9 pass on MI355X (gfx950, Triton 3.8). Includes an op benchmark.

### Motivation
  The Qwen3-Next GDN (gated delta-net) **prefill** is a four-kernel chain today:
  `causal_conv1d_split_qkv` → fused gating → the fp32 chunked delta-rule scan →
  gated RMSNorm + per-head group-128 FP8 quant. Four launches means the large
  intermediate tensors (split qkv, conv output, gated core) round-trip through HBM
  between every step.

  This PR adds a single fused Gluon op, `fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz`, that folds that
  work intra-kernel: split + conv + SiLU + QK-norm + gating-prep in one launch, the
  fp32 chunked scan, and a gated-RMSNorm + group-128 FP8-quant **epilogue**. The win
  is the intra-launch fusion and the dropped intermediate HBM traffic. The FP8
  activations a block-FP8 `out_proj` consumes are emitted by the epilogue launch, so
  there is no separate quantization kernel.

  This is the **prefill sibling of the decode kernel** (ROCm/aiter#5520): same
  Qwen3-Next GDN math, but it consumes ragged variable-length batches
  (`cu_seqlens` + `has_initial_state`) and runs the fp32 chunked scan instead of the
  single-token recurrent update.

  ### Design
  - **Reported, not asserted.** `fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz_supported(...) -> (bool, reason)`
    gates on **gfx950** (CDNA buffer addressing / inline asm / explicit register
    layouts) and **Triton ≥ 3.8** (the tiles are the Gluon dialect; some ROCm 3.7
    builds import `triton.experimental.gluon` but fail to compile it, so the gate is a
    version check, not just an import probe). Callers fall back to the four-kernel
    chain instead of crashing.
  - **Lazy tile import** on the dispatch path, so the module and the support predicate
    stay importable on any platform (older Triton, non-gfx950, CUDA).
  - Prefill spans a wide token range, so it dispatches one of **four autotuned M-tile
    schedules** over the covered region (`tokens ∈ [1024, 16384]`, `batch ∈ [1, 64]`).
  - Constraints inherited from the epilogue: `head_k_dim == head_v_dim == 128`, group
    size 128, `num_v_heads == 2·num_k_heads`.

  ```python
  (normalized_bf16, conv_state, delta_state, quantized_fp8, scales) = fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz(
      projected_qkvz, projected_ba, conv_state, delta_state,
      cache_indices, cu_seqlens, has_initial_state,
      conv_weight, conv_bias, a_log, dt_bias, norm_weight,
      scale=head_k_dim ** -0.5, eps=norm.eps,
  )   # conv_state / delta_state advanced in place
  ```

  ### Files changed (9 files, +4655)
  | File | + | What |
  |------|---|------|
  | `aiter/ops/triton/gated_delta_net/fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz.py` | 308 | Public op + `_supported()` gate + tile
  dispatch (`_select_tile_key`) |
  | `aiter/ops/triton/_gluon_kernels/gfx950/gated_delta_net/fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz/` | 3761 | 4 Gluon M-tile schedules
  (`_tile_m1024_3071`, `_tile_m3072_16384`, `_tile_m12289_16384_b1_5`, `_tile_m12289_16384_b6_15`) + package `__init__`
  |
  | `aiter/ops/triton/gated_delta_net/__init__.py` | 6 | Export `fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz` / `_supported` |
  | `op_tests/triton_tests/test_fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz.py` | 416 | Correctness vs pure-torch fp32 reference |
  | `op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz.py` | 164 | Latency benchmark |

  ### Accuracy — run command
  Correctness is checked against a **pure-torch fp32 sequential-scan reference**
  (deliberately *not* the chunked algorithm the kernel uses, so agreement is
  meaningful), matched to the kernel's bf16 rounding boundaries. Needs a gfx950 +
  Triton ≥ 3.8 ROCm environment.

  ```bash
  # from the aiter checkout, on an MI350-series (gfx950) host:
  python3 -m pytest -q op_tests/triton_tests/test_fused_gdn_prefill_qkvz.py
  ```
  Result on MI355X (Triton 3.8): **9 passed** — all 4 M-tiles compile+run+match the
  reference, both `has_initial_state` paths, determinism, and the unsupported-reason
  path. Numerics: fp8 activation ~1.3–7% (fp8 level), `conv_state` exact, recurrent
  state ~0.4%.

  ### Perf

  **Kernel vs the four-kernel chain it replaces** (MI355X, num_k=4 / num_v=8 /
  head=128; latency ms, median; speedup of the fused kernel):

  | shape k:v:b:s |     m | 4-kernel chain (ms) | fused (ms) | speedup |
  |---------------|------:|--------------------:|-----------:|--------:|
  | 4:8:1:4096    |  4096 |               0.691 |      0.222 |   3.1×  |
  | 4:8:2:4096    |  8192 |               0.834 |      0.302 |   2.8×  |
  | 4:8:4:2048    |  8192 |               0.782 |      0.287 |   2.7×  |
  | 4:8:1:8192    |  8192 |               0.867 |      0.324 |   2.7×  |
  | 4:8:1:2048    |  2048 |               0.616 |      0.215 |   2.9×  |
  | 4:8:2:1024    |  2048 |               0.677 |      0.176 |   3.8×  |
  | 4:8:8:1024    |  8192 |               0.744 |      0.209 |   3.6×  |
  | 4:8:2:8192    | 16384 |               1.072 |      0.509 |   2.1×  |

  (2.1–3.8× faster; widest at small-seq/large-batch where launch overhead dominates,
  narrowest at m=16384 where it is compute-bound.)

  **End-to-end through sglang** (Qwen3-Next-80B FP8, MI355X, TP4), prefill-focused
  (ISL 6144 / OSL 8) so TTFT surfaces the prefill win:

  | metric | stock | fused | Δ |
  |--------|------:|------:|---|
  | Median TTFT (ms) | 647.9 | 471.6 | **−27%** |
  | Input throughput (tok/s) | 92.8k | 125.4k | **+35%** |
  | GSM8K | 0.955 | 0.950 | parity |

  A balanced 1k/1k concurrency sweep (1→32) is TTFT-neutral-to-better (−12–16% at low
  concurrency, −2–6% at high), decode-neutral (TPOT identical), GSM8K parity
  (0.953 / 0.950). The sglang consumer wiring is a companion PR.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Unify GEMM tuning through config lookup
body:
Replace separate GEMM tuning harnesses and post-processing scripts with one config-lookup driver and 40 input-building cases. Each architecture/backend uses its own DEFAULT.json keys; kernel authors own that contract and can constrain search values per case.

The driver profiles the current config and candidates with rocprofv3. It sums selected GEMM and split-K reduction kernel durations per invocation, then takes the median of 250 cold-cache runs. Warmup, Python/wrapper overhead, cache clears and output resets are excluded. Each config runs in a fresh process with a configurable timeout; failures are logged with the exact config and compiler/driver output, and the next config still runs. This simple isolation has more process startup overhead than the old batched sweep.

Save the best working config when it is faster than the current config, or when no tuned M bucket exists. Preserve other buckets. Output checks use a deterministic reference from the current config when available. Both backends can be requested with --backend both and are tuned separately; omitted backend selection follows the wrapper default, including Gluon preference on supported gfx1250 routes. Triton can still be selected explicitly. The observed lookup handles gfx942, gfx950, gfx1250 and future supported architectures without another tuner.

Add backend selection to the FP4 preshuffle wrapper and document kernel coverage, author requirements and the differences from the old workflow. Remove the CPU unit-test file as requested. Shared Triton pruning/tile blacklisting, old screen-log/CLI compatibility, multi-shape log aggregation, verify-only command and throughput printing are not carried forward. MoE/grouped GEMMs with different loaders remain outside this tuner.

Validation: Black, Ruff, Python compilation, --list and git diff --check pass. An ad hoc synthetic-trace/simulated-process smoke check verifies main+reduction timing, exclusion of warmup/cache work, incomplete-trace rejection, failure logs and continuation after crashes/timeouts. No CPU unit-test file was retained. GPU correctness, real rocprofv3 integration and Linux process-group termination are unverified on this Windows host, so this PR remains draft.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Unify afp8wfp8 GEMM kernels
body:
## Summary

Generalize `gemm_afp8wfp8` to support compact E8M0 scales with activation groups of 32 or 128 and weight scale blocks of **1×32, 32×32, or 128×128**.

This replaces the separate group32 kernel implementation with shared AFP8WFP8 execution paths, reducing duplicated kernel, dispatch, and tuning logic.

## Implementation

- Parameterize scale indexing and broadcasting by activation and weight scale-group sizes.
- Support ordinary and packed-K execution, including fused split-K reduction, through configuration-based dispatch.
- Keep separate configuration families for each scale layout and tune the gfx950 configurations.
- Preserve the group32 entry point as a thin compatibility wrapper.
- Remove the duplicate group32 kernels and obsolete configs.
- Consolidate kernel tests and benchmarks into the AFP8WFP8 files, including an option to benchmark all 1,224 group32 PR shapes.

The existing preshuffle implementation remains available.

## Performance

Measured on **AMD Instinct MI355X / gfx950**, using BF16 outputs and alternating baseline/shared-kernel CUDA graph timings.

Speedups are geometric means relative to the corresponding original implementation.

| Path | Cases | Speedup | Regressions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Group32 overall | 1,224 | 1.0471× | 1 |
| Group32 ordinary | 1,074 | 1.0547× | 1 |
| Group32 packed-K | 150 | 0.9941× | 0 |
| Original AFP8 normal | 64 | 1.1111× | 0 |
| Original AFP8 preshuffle | 64 | 1.0003× | 0 |

A regression is defined as:

```text
shared latency > baseline latency × 1.05 + 0.5 µs
```

One group32 ordinary case exceeds this threshold:

| M | N | K | Baseline | Shared | Excess over threshold |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 16,384 | 1,280 | 4.805 µs | 5.867 µs | 0.322 µs |

This regression reproduced in independent runs on two GPUs.

## Validation

- **1,224 group32 shapes and 128 original AFP8 cases passed numerical checks.**
- Group32 validation compares complete outputs against the preserved implementation and checks independent FP64 references—full for small shapes and sampled for large shapes.
- Original AFP8 validation uses full dequantized FP32 references.
- **346 correctness/interface tests passed; 14 architecture-specific tests skipped.**

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Attention] Add overflow-guarded per-call int32 varlen strides
body:
## Summary

AITER's Triton variable-length attention currently selects 32- vs 64-bit stride arithmetic through process-global state. This PR adds a **per-call** opt-in so a caller can request 32-bit addressing when the complete launch is safe, without changing other concurrent attention calls.

`prefer_int32_strides=True` uses the int32 specialization only when the checked tensor layout and launch geometry fit safely in int32. Otherwise the existing int64 path is used or, for unsupported metadata/implementations, the opt-in is rejected explicitly.

Defaults are unchanged.

## Safety boundary

The opt-in is currently limited to BF16 inference, matching the qualified use case. FP16/FP32 keep the existing int64 dispatch, as does training.

The guard covers:

- Q/K/V, output and LSE storage offsets and strides
- production tile sizes
- padded and one-past tile coordinates
- sequence-coordinate and sliding-window arithmetic
- flattened launch-grid bounds
- 1D contiguous cumulative-length metadata

Unsupported implementations such as Gluon/DAO do not silently ignore the request.

## Validation

The current test suite runs the new branch in the normal Triton attention pytest path. On MI300X/gfx942, **307 tests pass** across the bounds/configuration suite and GPU dispatch/parity cases. The GPU cases cover output and LSE, graph replay, causal/windowed attention, GQA, strided views, head padding and independent FP32 references. FP16/FP32 fallback is also checked.

For the long MiniMax H3 attention shape that motivated this work, the isolated primitive improved from **134.90 ms to 84.80 ms (1.59x)**.

With the companion SGLang adapter (#39249), a matched 8x MI300X MiniMax H3 run with Cache-DiT off improved full generation time from **208.17 s to 142.12 s**, or **46.48% more serial clips/hour**. The three measured decoded audio/video outputs were identical between the two arms.

Short attention shapes can regress, so this PR does not enable the option by default or claim a universal speedup.

## Review question

The main maintainer question is whether the per-call API and its safety/fallback boundary are the right abstraction for Triton varlen attention. The implementation does not change the attention algorithm or remove overflow protection.

title: [Triton] unified_attention 2D: optional block skipping (BLASST)
body:
# [Triton] unified_attention 2D: optional block skipping (BLASST)

## Motivation

Adds opt-in dynamic block sparsity to `kernel_unified_attention_2d`, following BLASST (arXiv:2512.12087) - a dynamic sparse attention mechanism that reuses online softmax statistics to identify negligible attention scores, skipping softmax, value block loads, and the subsequent matrix multiplication. Off by default and inert when off.

On long-context prefill a large fraction of K/V tiles contribute nothing after softmax normalisation. Because the running maximum is already maintained by the online softmax, identifying those tiles needs no pre-computation, no proxy scores and no training - only a comparison against a threshold.

Measured on Qwen3-8B / RULER at 32K context: **1.2475× at 45.0% achieved tile elision**, with no change whatsoever to the dense path.

## Technical Details

### API

```python
unified_attention(..., block_skip_threshold=0.0, skip_counter=None)
```

| | |
|---|---|
| `block_skip_threshold` | `0.0` disables. Above 0, the threshold λ against which `tile_max - running_max` is compared. |
| `skip_counter` | optional `int32[2]`, accumulated in place as `[tiles visited, tiles elided]`. Passing a buffer is the opt-in; there is no flag and no module-level state. |

λ is model- and sequence-length-dependent and must be calibrated. The counter exists so a caller can check that their threshold elides anything at all.

### The skip decision

Per K/V tile, when enabled:

```python
skip     = (s_max - M) < log2_threshold       # M is the max BEFORE this tile
all_skip = tl.sum(skip.to(tl.int32)) == BLOCK_M
if not (ENABLE_BLOCK_SKIP and all_skip):
    ... compute exactly as dense, for every row ...
```

Three details are load-bearing:

**The decision is per tile, not per row.** A tile that survives the vote is computed exactly as dense. `test_no_elision_is_dense_within_rounding` holds the kernel to this.

**The comparison is against the running maximum BEFORE the tile**, not the value after folding in the current tile. The latter is equivalent for λ < 1 but reduces to `0 < log2(λ)` above it, which skips every tile including the one holding the maximum. `test_no_nan_above_unity` guards it.

**The V load is deferred** behind the skip decision when the feature is on, so an elided tile never touches V. That is where the bandwidth saving comes from.

Both tile loops are patched, including the `SPLIT_UNMASKED_LOOP` variant. The unmasked loop holds nearly all elidable tiles on long prefill.

### Nothing changes when it is off

`ENABLE_BLOCK_SKIP` and `PRELOAD_V` are `tl.constexpr`, so at the default threshold every addition folds away at compile time. `log2_threshold` is a runtime scalar rather than a constexpr so that sweeping thresholds does not recompile per value.

### Scheduling

Enabling the threshold also enables descending-q ordering and an atomic work ticket. Both are gated on it and neither touches the dense path.

The 2D grid is `(num_kv_heads, total_num_q_blocks)` and the hardware places workgroup `w` on `XCD w % 8`, so at 8 KV heads on 8 XCDs every workgroup for a head is pinned to one chiplet - verified on hardware by reading `HW_REG_XCC_ID` for all 8192 workgroups. That costs nothing while every head does the same work. Skipping is what makes per-head cost data-dependent, and then the launch waits on whichever chiplet drew the densest head. These exist to repair a problem skipping introduces.

They only permute which workgroup computes which tile, so the result is bitwise unchanged. Tickets are head-major, and the order is not arbitrary - a q-major decode measures slower.

### Not supported

Silently disabled, because a caller enabling this once for a whole model still reaches this wrapper on every step:

- **decode** (`ALL_DECODE`) - one query row per sequence, nothing to be far below
- **sliding window** - a fully-masked row leaves the running maximum at `-inf`, which the sanitizer rewrites to `0.0`, changing what the comparison means
- **the 3D path** - segments restart the running maximum, so the first tile of each can never skip; different semantics, out of scope here

Rejected loudly:

- **the Gluon backend** - asserts rather than ignoring the threshold, so a caller cannot believe they asked for sparsity and silently measure dense

### Env vars

Both default to the shipping configuration and exist for rollback and A/B:

| | |
|---|---|
| `AITER_UA_BLASST_SCHED=0` | disable the scheduling, keep skipping |
| `AITER_UA_BLASST_PRELOAD_V=1` | keep V hoisted instead of deferring it |

## Test Plan

**Existing suite, unchanged.** `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_unified_attention.py` run in full (non-Gluon) to confirm the dense path is unaffected.

**New suite.** `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_unified_attention_blasst.py`, 16 tests, reusing `generate_data` and `ref_paged_attn` from the existing suite so the inputs and the reference match:

- threshold 0 matches the reference and is bitwise identical to omitting the argument
- no elision means no approximation, within floating-point reassociation
- degradation is bounded and monotonic in λ
- λ ∈ {1.001 … 12.0} stay finite
- decode, sliding window and 3D-routed shapes fall back to dense, bitwise
- the Gluon path raises
- scheduling on/off is bitwise identical
- the elision counter is wired, monotonic, untouched when disabled, and rejects a bad buffer

A guard asserts the test shape actually reaches the 2D kernel; a shape routing to 3D would pass every test while exercising nothing.

**Codegen.** `blasst_repro/codegen_diff.sh` compiles this branch and the pre-change sources and diffs the emitted AMDGCN, to check the claim that the feature costs nothing when off at the instruction level rather than by timing.

**Benchmark.** `blasst_repro/bench_blasst_ua2d.py` sweeps λ on random inputs and reports achieved elision beside every speedup, taken from the kernel's own counter. `blasst_repro/README.md` has the full reproduction steps; no dataset is required.

**End-to-end.** Qwen3-8B / RULER, 13 tasks × 50 prompts × 36 layers at 32K context, λ = 0.02878, timing dense against the feature on for every (prompt, layer) pair.

## Test Result

**Existing suite:** 1088 passed, 1056 skipped, 0 failed.

**New suite:** 16 passed, 3 skipped (gfx1250-only), 0 failed. Verified with the chain-dot patch both enabled and disabled.

**Codegen with the feature off: identical emitted code** - same 1,181 lines, same instruction stream, sgpr 100 / vgpr 206 / zero spills on both. The only difference is the kernel signature, where `log2_threshold` and `num_q_blocks` are runtime scalars, growing the kernarg segment 184 → 192 bytes and shifting the offsets after them. No instruction loads either with skipping off.

**Random inputs**, MI355X, 32 query heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, seqlen 16384, dense baseline 2.950 ms:

| λ | speedup | achieved elision | relative error |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-9 | 0.899× | 0.0% | 0.000 |
| 0.02878 | 0.898× | 0.0% | 0.000 |
| 0.1 | 0.901× | 0.0% | 0.000 |
| 0.3 | 0.908× | 0.0% | 0.000 |
| 1 | 1.033× | 21.4% | 0.245 |
| 1.5 | 1.274× | 54.8% | 0.656 |
| 2 | 1.433× | 70.9% | 1.025 |
| 4 | 1.684× | 90.2% | 2.214 |

These results show: The **overhead floor**: at a threshold that elides nothing the skip check costs about 10%, so the feature has to elide before it pays. And the **conversion ceiling**: once tiles are actually being dropped, speedup rises with elision to 1.68× at 90%. Relative error is exactly 0 wherever elision is 0: a tile that survives the vote is computed as dense, so nothing is approximated until something is skipped.

**End-to-end**, MI355X (gfx950), bf16, 23,400 (prompt, layer) measurements:

| | |
|---|---|
| speedup vs dense | **1.2475×** |
| achieved tile elision | **45.0%** |
| measurements at or above 1.0× | 21,245 / 23,400 (90.8%) |
| relative error vs dense | 0.0349 mean, 0.2340 max |
| non-finite outputs | 0 |

Speedup tracks achieved elision closely, and both vary by task and by layer. Per-task and per-layer breakdowns available on request.

Measurements were taken in the environment under `blasst_repro/`, which pins the Triton build; see its README.

body:
## Motivation

Currently, triton benchmarks rely on triton.testing.do_bench but its defaults are not very accurate isolating per kernel times. This PR introduces a new bench. utility that uses torch profiler under the hood and can better strip out the wrapper overhead. Under cuda-graph, the wrapper overhead is rarely seen in traces so measuring actual kernel time provides a more accurate signal.

It also supports l2 cache flushing and rotating buffers to simulate cold cache runtime.

I changed the profiler for bench_fp8_mqa_logits.py to the new one to use as an example.
 ## Technical Details
Adds `do_bench_profiler()` in `op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/utils/profiler_bench.py`. It runs `fn` under `torch.profiler`, keeps only the device events whose name matches one of the kernel names you pass, groups the launches back into iterations and reduces across them. Returns per-iteration milliseconds, same unit as `do_bench`, so it drops into existing scripts without rescaling.

- `num_warmup` / `num_iters` are literal iteration counts, not `do_bench`'s ms budgets.
- `flush_l2` (on by default) with `cache_size_mb` (512).
- `data_gen` + `num_copies` build rotating input sets up front as an alternative to flushing. Iteration `i` gets copy `i % num_copies`, called as `fn(*data)` for a tuple, `fn(**data)` for a dict, else `fn(data)`.
- `return_mode` takes mean/median/min/max or any percentile (`p25`, `p50`, `p90`, ...). Pass a list to get several statistics out of a single run instead of re-benchmarking per statistic. `RETURN_MODES` is exported for use as argparse choices.
- `per_kernel=True` returns a dict keyed by filter name rather than the aggregate, which is the multi-kernel breakdown.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [JIT] fix(jit): baton liveness is undecidable from pid+host under --network host
body:
Fixes #5266.

## The bug

`FileBaton` records its holder as **pid + hostname**. A container started with `docker run --network host` — the normal way to run a tuner — reports the **host's** hostname while keeping its **own PID namespace**, and every container has a pid 1 and low worker pids (100-104).

So when a tuner container is killed mid-build, the next container reads the leaked lock, sees a matching hostname, checks `os.kill(103, 0)`, finds **its own worker** at pid 103, and concludes the dead holder is alive. Its workers then wait forever:

```
[pid=101 pname=SpawnPoolWorker-1] waiting for baton release at
    .../lock_module_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_cktile_tune
```

With a host-mounted build cache the leak survives container restarts, so the wedge is **permanent** until someone deletes the file by hand. "Delete the lock files first" became a required step in our tuning runbook.

## The fix

Record the **PID namespace** (`/proc/self/ns/pid`) and the holder's **start time** (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22) alongside pid and host:

| holder | decision |
|---|---|
| same namespace | pid alive **and** start time matches → live. This also closes the pid-reuse hole on any host. |
| other namespace | the pid is meaningless here, so decide on a **heartbeat**: the holder touches the lock every `heartbeat_seconds` while it works; a lock untouched for `heartbeat_stale_seconds` (default 60 s) is stale. |
| different host | unchanged — never steal. |

Locks written by an older AITER carry two lines; they parse with empty ns/start-time and keep exactly the previous behaviour.

## Checked

Self-held lock never looks stale · foreign-namespace holder with a live local pid is respected **while heartbeating** and goes stale when it stops · recycled pid caught via start time · dead pid · legacy 2-line locks (live and dead) · 0-byte orphan grace unchanged · `wait()` returns False after breaking a stale lock · heartbeat observed touching the file.

Same campaign as #5262 / #5268 / #5263–#5265.

title: [FlyDSL] [Bugfix] Route a16w4 SiLU MoE to CK-Tile and apply swiglu_limit
body:
## Motivation

A bf16-activation x MXFP4-weight SiLU MoE with a `swiglu_limit` has no working route. This is the small-batch path that DeepSeek-V4.1 takes on gfx950 whenever the token count is below `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND` (default 256). `get_2stage_cfgs` only sends SwiGLU to CK-Tile there, so SiLU falls through to CK2stages. CK2stages has no A16W4 SiLU instance and no clamp. In our container the JIT build of `module_moe_ck2stages_b16_fp4x2_preshuffle_on_b16_silu_per_1x32_mulWeightStage2` fails at server start. Where it builds, `swiglu_limit` would be dropped.

Downstream, sgl-project/sglang#39857 carries this change as a Docker patch, and DeepSeek-V4.1 deployments set `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0` to stay on the a8w4 route. This PR lets both go.

## Technical Details

- `get_2stage_cfgs`: SiLU with bf16 output on gate/up-interleaved MXFP4 weights takes the CK-Tile split-K post-activation route that SwiGLU already uses. SwiGLU keeps its `standard` post-activation layout; SiLU uses `auto`, which selects the interleaved FlyDSL activation for fp4 weights.
- `fused_moe_2stages`: forwards `swiglu_limit` to `cktile_moe_stage1` for that SiLU case.
- `cktile_moe_stage1` and `flydsl_silu_and_mul_interleaved`: take `swiglu_limit` and pass it to the kernel (`runtime_swiglu_limit`) instead of a fixed `inf`.
- The SiLU route is limited to `GateMode.INTERLEAVE`. On separated gate/up weights the output was about 4.5% (cosine) off the clamped reference, so that layout is left as it was.

## Test Plan

```bash
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=256 python -m pytest op_tests/test_moe_a16w4_silu_limit.py -q
```

The new test runs a DeepSeek-V4.1-shaped MoE (model_dim 5120, inter_dim 2304, 32 experts, top-6, `swiglu_limit=7`) through `fused_moe` and compares it with the clamped `torch_moe_stage1/2` reference. It also checks that the inputs actually reach the limit.

## Test Result

MI350X VF (gfx950), ROCm 10 Python wheels with torch 2.11. Current main does not JIT-build in this container (`module_moe_asm`), so the change was validated on `acf8fdf93`, where it applies unchanged.

| | token=1 | token=32 |
|---|---|---|
| without this change | JIT build failure | JIT build failure |
| with this change (cosine diff vs clamped ref) | 1.3e-5 | 1.4e-5 |

title: [OPUS] Speed up the gfx1250 32mx1 MLA sparse-prefill kernels
body:
## Summary

Rebuilds the two prebuilt gfx1250 code objects that serve `16 < H_Q <= 32` on the DSv4 sparse-prefill path, and reworks the op test so its inputs match how the kernel is actually used in a DSA deployment.

## Kernels

`opus_mla_v4_prefill_a8w8_32mx1_16nx4` now fits two workgroups per CU: LDS drops from 224256 to 157696 bytes (154 KiB, under the 160 KiB half-budget) and the VGPR count from 734 to 512. `opus_mla_v4_prefill_a16w16_32mx1_16nx4` prefetches V one tile ahead in the round loop, trading VGPRs (742 -> 826) for a shorter dependency chain.

Measured with `op_tests/test_pa_sparse_prefill.py --backend opus --h_q 32` across `prec x {1024, 4096} tokens x {1024, 2048} topk x {64Ki, 1Mi} pages`, 16 points per precision:

| precision | min | max | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bf16 | 1.005x | 1.029x | 1.022x |
| fp8 | 1.077x | 1.300x | 1.207x |

The fp8 gain narrows as the prefix pool grows (1.23-1.30x at 64Ki pages, 1.08-1.19x at 1Mi), which is what an occupancy win looks like once the gather starts missing cache. Accuracy is unchanged: every point reports a 0.0 mismatch ratio against the PyTorch reference.

## Test

The page table now models a DeepSeek Sparse Attention top-k selection instead of uniform-random CSR rows. Each token draws `topk` rows from each range, the extend range is causal (token `i` only sees `[0, i]`, since those rows are the chunk's own K/V), and indices stay scattered so the gather does not degenerate into a near-sequential read. This replaces the `sparse` / `dense` / `empty` modes; `--topk` and `--total_pages` become the sweep axes, with `total_pages` defaulting to `[65536, 1048576]` so the gather is measured outside the caches rather than partly served by L2.

Two hardening changes come with it. Pool rows the page table never names are filled with NaN (0xFF for fp8 NoPE, which is NaN as both e4m3 and E8M0), so a gather that walks off its index list cannot return plausible numbers. The fp8 row pad past the block scales is 0xFF for the same reason. All three backends (`opus`, `triton`, `asm`) pass with both in place.

`_PYTEST_CASES` folds `topk` into each case rather than crossing it as an axis, which kept most combinations from collapsing onto the same whole-pool budget. The seven cases cover every wave layout, both cluster widths, two partial head blocks, a ragged KV tile tail, a whole-pool budget, and empty pools.

title: [FlyDSL] Refactor PA decode and load CSV tuning results
body:
Refactor the monolithic FlyDSL PA decode kernel into operation classes following `fmha_gfx950`, and let the PA interface consume offline workgroup-budget recommendations from CSV.

- Split schedule/traits, context, memory movement, GEMM, softmax, epilogue, and pipeline components. Carry forward dense planned query splitting, eligible unsigned FP8 buffer addressing between 2 and 4 GiB, K/V prefetch scheduling, and compact/window-bounded reductions.
- Store complete tuning results in one CSV: readable shape/budget/performance columns plus structured payload cells preserve raw timing samples, accuracy checks, failures, and source fingerprints. Loading validates the row hierarchy and displayed values. `--output results.csv` is the output path; `--csv` is an alias. Dry-run output is also CSV.
- Add `load_tuned_results()` to the PA interface. It caches an immutable index of validated recommendations, checks current source fingerprints, and rejects ambiguous recommendations for the same device-local geometry. The default path is `aiter/configs/model_configs/flydsl_pa_decode_tuned.csv`; an absent default gives no recommendations. Explicit missing or malformed files raise an error, and `reload=True` refreshes the index.

Omitting `max_context_partition_num` and `work_plan` enables automatic eager planning:

```python
pa_decode(
    ...,
    max_context_partition_num=None,
    tuned_file="results.csv",
    max_context_length=max_context_length,
)
```

The host context bound and local tensor geometry select the recommendation. Missing, stale, conflicting, or unmatched recommendations use the default budget of `2 * CU`; attention with sinks also uses the default because the tuner measures attention without sinks. The host bound controls page-rounded planned scheduling, so padded block tables retain the measured query-splitting policy. Callers must ensure GPU context lengths do not exceed that bound; matching does not read lengths back from the GPU.

Explicit integer partition counts retain static execution. Explicit work plans take precedence and can supply their partition cap when the argument is omitted. For graph capture or preallocated scratch, load the CSV and use `results.lookup_budget(shape, architecture, num_cu)` to prepare a plan before capture, then pass `work_plan` and the matching context bound. Automatic planning is rejected during capture.

Validation of the CSV/API change:

- 62 CPU checks pass, covering complete CSV roundtrips, malformed/truncated/duplicate data, CLI output, atomic replacement, cache/reload behavior, immutable results, source/accuracy rejection, and local-shape conflicts. These harnesses exercise the actual codec and loader definitions without GPU imports.
- 144 independent offline scheduling-bound checks pass across page sizes 16/64/128 and automatic, explicit-plan, and static modes. The gfx950 B4/QL4/G16/D128/L4096/budget256 example selects identical complete schedules for compact and padded tables when given the same host bound.
- Black, Ruff, and diff checks pass. `op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py` adds 11 host test cases and two GPU integration cases for automatic planning, fallback, padded tables, explicit-plan precedence, and graph replay. The existing 242 native cases are retained.
- **GPU validation of this update remains unexecuted:** all eight available remote MI355 devices retained other workloads, and the local gfx942 probe blocked in HIP initialization before PA/FlyDSL code ran. No new GPU accuracy, throughput, or regression result is claimed. Frozen snapshots, verified source manifests, and guarded accuracy/performance launchers are prepared for a rerun.

The kernel operation files are unchanged by the CSV/API update. Earlier validation at `a24ea4967`, against the optimized monolithic implementation `7f3d014cd`, passed 242/242 native cases on each revision. Across 35 offline gfx950/gfx942 tile specializations, location-stripped MLIR, complete HSACO, and register/LDS/spill metadata matched. gfx942 coverage in that comparison was offline only.

The earlier MI355/gfx950 target comparison used batch 200, QL4, Hkv1/G16, D128, page128, transposed V, BF16 Q/output, per-token FP8 KV, and contexts from 4 to 200000:

| Workgroup budget | Monolithic `7f3d014cd` median (µs) | Validated `a24ea4967` median (µs) | Validated logical KV TB/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 | 1135.582 | 1139.307 | 4.494 |
| 2048 | 973.574 | 973.608 | **5.259** |

Each row is a separate paired run. Timing includes decode and reduction and excludes loading/planning, JIT, allocation, quantization, and reference calculation. Logical KV throughput counts 5,120,077,056 K+V bytes once per call, without a QL multiplier, using `bytes / (median_us * 1e6)`.

**Known precision limitation from that comparison:** `varlen_b81_q4_c1027` (batch 81, QL4, Hkv1/G16, D128/page128, per-token FP8 KV, contexts 4–1027) fails the strict FP32-reference check at `atol=rtol=0.005` on both validated revisions: 38 elements exceed tolerance, with maximum absolute error 0.00712435. Outputs are byte-identical. This failure was retained and excluded from timing; tolerances were not changed.

title: [DSv4] Tuned decode moe kernels for mori-EP backend- #41119
body:
## Motivation

Prefill and decode send tokens to very different experts. On DeepSeek-V4 EP8, decode concentrates on a few hot experts, while prefill spreads almost evenly. The same MoE shape therefore wants different kernels in each case.

A single tuned table can't express that. The tuned key uses only the padded token count, and prefill and decode fall into the same buckets. Whichever resolves a bucket first fixes the kernel for both through `get_2stage_cfgs`' `lru_cache`. With CUDA graphs that is always decode, because every bucket is resolved during decode graph capture. The only way to tune decode today is to force the same kernels onto prefill.

This PR lets the caller say whether each call is prefill or decode (the "regime"), and gives each regime its own optional table.

## Summary of changes

- **`aiter/fused_moe.py`**
  - Adds `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE_PREFILL` and `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE_DECODE`, which name a tuned table per regime.
  - Adds `set_moe_regime()`, `get_moe_regime()` and the `moe_regime()` context manager for the host to select the active regime.
  - `get_2stage_cfgs` takes `moe_regime` as an argument, so it becomes part of the cache key. The two regimes get separate cache entries instead of overwriting each other. Both runtime callers (`fused_moe_` and `fused_moe_2stages`) pass the active regime.
  - A regime table replaces the default table but keeps the normal lookup behaviour: activation and tier fallbacks, and the heuristic when a shape is missing. It deliberately does not go through the `config_file=` path, which errors when a shape is missing.
  - When neither env var is set, or the host never sets a regime, behaviour is unchanged and the single `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` table is used.
- **`aiter/configs/model_configs/moe_regime/dsv4_fp8fp4_ep8_tuned_fmoe_decode.csv`**
  - The decode table for DSV4-Pro FP4 on gfx950 with EP8 and shared-expert fusion (expert=49), token buckets 512 to 16384.
  - Stage1 is tuned against decode's real routing. Stage2 is left on the default geometry.
  - It lives in a subdirectory on purpose. aiter merges every top-level `model_configs/*tuned_fmoe*.csv` into the default table, which would apply the decode kernels to prefill too.
- **`aiter/configs/model_configs/moe_regime/README.md`**
  - Explains that tables in this directory are not merged into the default table, and which env var selects each one.

The host-side change, which sets the regime on each forward pass and pins decode during CUDA graph capture, is in a separate sglang PR.

## Results

Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 on 8Ã^W MI355X, ISL/OSL 8k/1k, concurrency 128, DP8/EP8 with MoRI a2a, DSpark MTP.

## Summary

Follow-up to #5350: add three gfx950/256 A4W4 tuned shapes for the Qwen3.8-27B GDN BA projection, `(M,N,K)=(2|4|24,96,5120)`. The earlier shape generator required N to be a multiple of 128 and omitted N=96. All three rows select the existing `f4gemm_bf16_per1x32Fp4_BpreShuffle_32x128` ASM kernel (kernel ID 21, splitK 0); no kernel implementation or dispatch code changes.

## Measurement and validation

- M=2: 5.5835 µs; M=24: 5.7666 µs, from the original AITER tuner on gfx950. M=4: **5.6658 µs**, measured separately with `run_perftest` using the tuner's `run_gemm_a4w4_blockscale_asm` candidate, 10 warmups and 101 iterations (the same profiling settings used in the full tuner). All three rows have `errRatio=0` against the FP4-dequantized torch reference.
- The broad M=4 tuner sweep faulted on a CK candidate; the isolated measurement invoked **only** the selected ASM kernel. On HIP devices 6 and 7, five M=4 seeds per device passed reference comparison with zero mismatches; kernel times ranged 5.6093–5.6687 µs. The committed M=4 timing, TFLOPS and bandwidth derive from the HIP-6 seed-0 profiler measurement, not from graph replay or the earlier unmeasured trial row.
- With the completed CSV mounted into the pinned image, `gemm_a4w4` selected kernel ID 21 for M=2, M=4, and M=24; five seeds for each shape passed production-op reference comparison on each of HIP 6 and 7, and graph-captured output passed for each shape. The CSV keeps logical K=5120 (FP4 storage has K/2 packed columns).
- `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_config_shape_collision -v`: **20 tests passed, zero skips** against a disposable copy of current ROCm/aiter main (`b3d0cf4e0`) with the three rows, using a torch-enabled gfx950 container. The guard exercises runtime merging of the canonical A4W4 CSV and all model-config CSVs. `git diff --check` passed.

## Serving observation and scope

In a pinned SGLang/Quark image, AITER logs confirmed the M=4,N=96,K=5120 row was selected during the trial. Serial baseline/trial TP1 serving runs on each of HIP 6 and 7 reduced batch-four decode **graph replay** time by 6.7–7.8% and increased observed output-token throughput by 6.7–7.2% (32 requests per run). Those runs mounted a trial table containing M=2, M=4 and M=24; they did **not** isolate the M=4 row's individual end-to-end effect. Graph replay time is not full request latency. Repeated token/logprob probes varied even within the same configuration, so these observations are not a claim of model-level output equivalence.

The benchmark image baked its own AITER CSV and set `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A4W4` to that baked path; merging this PR alone will not update that image. A refreshed image or mounted CSV is needed to consume these rows.
